title: System of quality management — Reed & Alvarez CPAs
instructions: Reed & Alvarez CPAs is designing its system of quality management under SQMS No. 1 and SQMS No. 2. Classify each policy by component, then evaluate the proposed engagement quality reviewers.

exhibits.title: Proposed firm policies
exhibits.content:
1. Partner compensation is tied to quality ratings as well as revenue.
2. Before accepting a client, the firm evaluates the integrity of its principal owners.
3. The firm buys audit software and trains staff to use it.
4. All staff confirm their independence annually in writing.
5. Selected completed engagements are inspected each year, and the root causes of findings are analyzed.
6. The firm requires consultation with the national office on complex revenue issues.
7. Quality objectives and quality risks are updated annually as the firm's practice changes.

exhibits.title: Proposed EQ reviewers for the Year 3 audit of Pinecrest Clinics
exhibits.content:
- **Hale** — engagement partner for Years 1 and 2 of the Pinecrest audit
- **Irwin** — senior manager on the Year 3 Pinecrest team
- **Jiang** — partner in another office with health-care expertise, no involvement with Pinecrest
- **Kerr** — engagement partner on Pinecrest four years ago (Year −1)

parts.prompt: Select the component each policy primarily addresses.

rows.label: 1. Compensation tied to quality
rows.explanation: Leadership's accountability and incentives support a culture of quality.

rows.label: 2. Evaluating owners' integrity
rows.explanation: Client integrity is evaluated before acceptance.

rows.label: 4. Annual independence confirmations
rows.explanation: Independence is a relevant ethical requirement.

rows.label: 5. Inspections and root-cause analysis
rows.explanation: Evaluating the system and remediating deficiencies.

rows.label: 6. Required consultation
rows.explanation: Consultation on difficult matters is part of engagement performance.

rows.label: 7. Updating objectives and risks
rows.explanation: Establishing objectives and identifying and assessing risks.

parts.prompt: May each person serve as the Year 3 EQ reviewer?

rows.label: Hale
rows.explanation: Engagement partner within the past two years; the cooling-off period has not passed.

rows.label: Irwin
rows.explanation: A member of the engagement team cannot be the EQ reviewer.

rows.label: Jiang
rows.explanation: Competent, objective, and not involved in the engagement.

rows.label: Kerr
rows.explanation: More than two years have passed since Kerr was engagement partner.

parts.prompt: Which excerpt (paraphrased for study) supports your conclusion about Hale?

excerpts.text: The firm's policies should require a cooling-off period of two years, or longer if required by ethical requirements, before an individual who served as engagement partner is appointed as the engagement quality reviewer.
The firm should establish quality objectives that address the acceptance and continuance of client relationships and specific engagements.
The engagement partner should take overall responsibility for managing and achieving quality on the audit engagement.
A member in public practice should be independent in the performance of professional services as required by standards promulgated by bodies designated by Council.

parts.explanation: SQMS No. 2 imposes the two-year cooling-off period for former engagement partners.
